summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a complex medical history including sclerosing mesenteritis, multiple abdominal surgeries, and G-tube dependence was readmitted two days after discharge due to a malfunctioning PICC line that could not be flushed and showed signs of cracking. Blood cultures from the line grew coagulase-negative staphylococcus, prompting admission for IV vancomycin therapy. The patient remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable with no signs of systemic infection. A new dual-lumen PICC line was successfully placed via the right brachial vein despite known brachiocephalic stenosis. TPN was resumed, and she continued home medications for chronic pain, fibromatosis, Sjogren’s, and anticoagulation. The infectious disease team recommended a two-week course of vancomycin with weekly trough and lab monitoring. She was discharged home with services to complete antibiotic therapy, resume outpatient care, and follow up with her ID specialist.
